The latest open-weights release using Mixture-of-Depths architecture just changed how I think about inference efficiency.

Instead of passing every single token through every layer in a Transformer, this approach dynamically routes compute. Tokens that require deeper contextual understanding get full processing, while straightforward tokens bypass heavy layers entirely.

This is not just a marginal speedup. By skipping unnecessary calculations on a per-token basis, we get a massive reduction in latency and memory bandwidth strain during long-context generation.

For local deployment and high-concurrency systems, saving compute on predictable tokens means we can actually run larger, smarter base models on constrained hardware without sacrificing final output quality.

Have you experimented with dynamic routing models yet, or are you still relying on standard dense architectures for production?
